definition: Obstinate means not yielding easily to argument or persuasion; stubbornly set on one's own position.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word obstinate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know obstinate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The obstinate goat would not budge from the garden path, whatever the farmer tried.

Stubborn is the everyday, milder word, and English happily applies it to things as well as people — a stubborn cough, a stubborn jar lid; obstinate is stronger, suggesting a person's determined, unreasonable refusal to yield to actual arguments.
Intractable is stronger than obstinate: an intractable person or problem cannot be managed or steered at all, by anyone.

Headstrong describes someone who charges ahead on their own will, brushing off advice before it is even finished. Obstinate digs in where headstrong rushes forward: the obstinate person refuses to yield to arguments, while the headstrong one refuses to hear them out. One blocks change; the other races past it.

Inflexible means unwilling to bend or adapt — said of rules, schedules, plans, and the people who enforce them without exception. Obstinate is more personal and more willful: an active refusal to yield to arguments and persuasion. A policy can be inflexible; only a mind can be obstinate.

Obstinate means not yielding easily to argument or persuasion; stubbornly set on one's own position.
The debate team had lost three rounds in a row using Lena's opening strategy.
Her teammates showed her the judges' scoresheets and proposed a different order of arguments.
The coach walked her through exactly where the strategy was leaking points.
Lena crossed her arms and announced that the team would open the same way in the final round, too.
Win or lose, she was too obstinate to change course.
Lena refuses to change her chosen course of action despite clear evidence and repeated arguments from everyone around her — that refusal to yield is what makes her obstinate.
neutral-to-disapproving; everyday and formal use
Obstinate is the general-purpose member of this unit's 'stubborn' trio: a broad refusal to change one's mind or course of action.
Obdurate is harsher and more literary, implying a heart hardened against pity itself, while adamant points at emphatic, vocal insistence on one specific point.

obstinate: Intractable is stronger than obstinate: an intractable person or problem cannot be managed or steered at all, by anyone.
Every summer the Ruiz family drove to the coast, and every summer Uncle Tomás insisted on the old canyon road.
This year his nieces showed him the traffic app, his brother printed the new bypass times, and a highway sign itself announced the faster route.
Tomás studied each piece of evidence carefully, nodded at the figures, and remained obstinate, turning onto the canyon road exactly as he had for thirty years.
It was not that he failed to follow the arguments — he could repeat them back perfectly — he simply would not be moved by them.
By August the family had stopped arguing and simply packed extra sandwiches for the long way around.
